data.markdown:
_Account POV. Drawing the org and overlaying our engagement._

Account POV for CorePay. Open opportunity in SFDC: CorePay - Enterprise 2026, stage negotiation, $142K, close date 2026-09-11.

Where engagement is concentrated: all three Gong calls (Discovery 2026-06-17, Pricing Review 2026-06-22, QBR 2026-06-24) have Chris Jones as the consistent external participant. He is flagged as champion and marked recently hired. Robert Smith (CHRO) joined the Discovery call. Nicole Anderson attended Discovery and the QBR. The Pricing Review added Nicole Williams and Stephanie Clark (People Operations Manager). No contact from Finance or Engineering has appeared on any call.

Coverage gaps: Priya Raman (VP Finance) and the Engineering team have no recorded engagement. Given that Chris Jones pushed on pricing economics at the Pricing Review (Gong, 2026-06-22), a Finance voice in the room at some point may be worth noting as an open question.

Champion: Chris Jones, Head of Total Rewards, reporting to Robert Smith per the org data (2026-08-05, confidence 0.85). He has been active on all three calls and raised both pay equity (Gong, 2026-07-04) and grade structure (Gong, 2026-07-03) by name.

Org structure observations: the data shows two people carrying the Head of Total Rewards title, Chris Jones and Daniel Davis, both at confidence 0.85 (org data, 2026-08-05). That may reflect a real dual-leader structure, a reporting ambiguity, or a data artifact. Daniel Davis appeared on the QBR but is not flagged as champion. Worth confirming how these two roles relate. There is also an open Director of Compensation role posted 2026-07-24 on LinkedIn (linkedin.com/jobs/view/49b2ddff), which signals the comp team is still being built out even mid-cycle.

Low-confidence rows to verify: Priya Raman VP Finance at 0.55, Tom Bradley Staff Engineer at 0.45, and Nicole Williams Senior HR Generalist at 0.50. Their titles and reporting lines should be treated as uncertain until confirmed.

Funding signals in the data show conflicting figures: a $100M Series B detected 2026-07-01 (Crunchbase), a $100M Series C detected 2026-07-28 (Crunchbase, lead Accel), and a $15M Series C detected 2026-07-30 (Crunchbase, lead a16z). The round labels and amounts are inconsistent across entries, so the actual capital structure is unclear from the data as it stands.
